blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Generating compositional 3D scenes from a single image requires recovering detailed object geometry and coherent spatial arrangements. Existing object-to-scene methods, including SAM3D and MIDI, extend object generation through image-context reasoning or inter-instance modeling. Coordinating objects remains challenging with limited scene-level supervision. Directly extending object-centric generators to entire scenes can degrade geometry and fail to preserve instance scale, orientation, and pose. We propose Bri3D, a framework bridging scene-level structural reasoning and object-level generative priors through instance-aware voxel scene anchors. Bri3D predicts a color-coded scene scaffold encoding coarse object geometry and spatial arrangements. Each instance is extracted as a scene anchor and refined into a pose-preserving, prior-compatible voxel support, enabling a frozen object generator to synthesize detailed textured geometry in the anchor-defined spatial reference. This coarse-to-fine design separates scene organization from object-scale detail synthesis, focusing scene-level training on spatial organization and anchor refinement while reusing pretrained object priors. Experiments demonstrate improvements in scene layout, object geometry, visual quality, and generalization. Bri3D predicts scene layouts efficiently; full scene generation is faster than SceneGen and SAM3D.

blocks.en: 1  Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Generating high-fidelity 3D indoor scenes from a single image
remains a long-standing challenge at the intersection of computer
vision, graphics, and embodied AI [ 30 , 26 , 6 , 10 , 41 ] .
Recent 3D generative models have achieved remarkable progress in
synthesizing realistic individual objects [ 44 , 37 , 34 , 36 , 39 , 42 , 22 , 38 , 4 ] .
Extending this progress to indoor scenes, however, remains difficult.
Unlike isolated object generation, scene reconstruction must jointly
recover detailed object geometry and a globally valid spatial
configuration governed by relative scale, orientation, support
relationships, and collision avoidance.

blocks.en:
Recent object-to-scene methods combine object priors with inter-instance
modeling or image-conditioned shape and pose inference [ 18 , 28 , 3 ] .
They improve scene composition, yet coordinating object geometry and
placement remains challenging: errors can produce intersections,
floating furniture, and inconsistent arrangements, as shown in
Fig. 1 (a). These difficulties become more pronounced as
object counts and spatial relationships grow more complex. Meanwhile,
compositional scene data remain limited in quantity and
diversity [ 7 , 12 ] , providing limited
supervision for jointly learning global arrangements and fine-grained
object geometry. This motivates a division of learning responsibilities:
scene-level supervision establishes a coherent scaffold, while a
pretrained object generator supplies detailed geometry and appearance
priors. An explicit spatial interface between these two capabilities
allows scene organization to guide detailed object synthesis.

These observations motivate a different route for transferring strong
object-level generative priors to scene generation. We use a shared
spatial scaffold as the intermediate representation connecting
scene-level structure with object-level generation. Such a
representation should establish globally coordinated layouts in
a shared scene space, while remaining decomposable into individual
instances that can be processed by a pre-trained object generator.
It should further retain the anchor-defined spatial reference of
each instance while providing sufficient object-scale resolution for
high-fidelity geometry and appearance synthesis.

blocks.en:
To bridge this gap, we propose Bri3D, an image-to-compositional 3D scene generation framework built upon a scene scaffold that serves as the intermediate representation between scene-level structure and object-level generation.
Bri3D therefore uses scene anchors to connect scene-level layout
learning with pretrained object-level detail synthesis, reducing the
need to learn both capabilities jointly from scene data.
Bri3D first constructs a unified, instance-aware scene scaffold. This
scaffold provides a globally coordinated structural anchor that jointly
captures coarse object geometry and spatial arrangements.
Specifically, the Scene Scaffold Generator predicts a
color-coded, instance-aware voxel scaffold from an RGB image and its
corresponding segmentation result. Since all foreground objects are generated
within a shared scene representation, their placements and coarse
geometry are jointly determined under a common scene context. The
predicted color labels separate the scaffold into coarse object voxel
clusters, each serving as a scene anchor for object-scale
refinement. The Anchored Voxel Refiner encodes each clustered voxel into a
structural latent and injects Gaussian noise to construct a scene-anchored latent initialization . Conditioned on the
corresponding image evidence, it denoises the latent into a
pose-preserving, prior-compatible voxel support. This support is then
processed by the frozen detail-synthesis module of a pre-trained object
generator to synthesize a high-fidelity textured 3D object. The
generated objects are finally transformed back to their scaffold-derived
spatial configurations and composed into the complete scene.

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1  3D Object Generation
blocks.zh: 2.1 三维对象生成

blocks.en:
Recent 3D object generators achieve high geometric fidelity by learning
from large-scale collections of isolated shapes. Existing methods mainly
use point-, voxel-, or mesh-based representations. Point-based methods,
such as 3DShape2VecSet [ 43 ] , encode unordered
point sets into compact latents, while diffusion and rectified-flow
models further improve generation quality and scalability [ 44 , 22 ] . Mesh-based methods model
surface connectivity and produce high-quality geometry, but
autoregressive decoding often incurs substantial inference cost [ 35 ] . Voxel-based methods provide explicit spatial structure and are
well suited for image-conditioned generation. TRELLIS [ 39 , 40 ] introduces Sparse Structured Latents that
combine sparse voxel supports with per-voxel features and support
decoding into multiple 3D representations. Subsequent methods further
improve geometric fidelity and efficiency [ 42 , 38 ] . However, these models are trained
on isolated, normalized shapes and lack the scene-level reasoning
required for object placement, scale, orientation, and spatial
coordination. Directly extending them to full-scene generation therefore
often degrades structural quality.

blocks.en: 2.2  Compositional 3D Scene Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 2.2 3D场面重建

blocks.en:
A common strategy for single-image scene reconstruction is to generate
or retrieve individual objects and place them in a shared 3D coordinate
system. Earlier methods rely on CAD retrieval and alignment [ 21 , 14 ] , while recent approaches use scene
graphs, geometric cues, or vision-language models to infer object
identities and spatial configurations [ 13 , 41 ] . Although these pipelines can
reuse high-quality assets, they depend heavily on monocular depth, pose,
and scale estimation. Errors propagate through registration and
assembly, producing floating objects, intersections, or inconsistent
layouts. Independently generated objects may also be geometrically
incompatible, limiting global scene coherence. SceneDreamer [ 5 ] learns unbounded 3D landscape generation
from 2D image collections through adversarial training. Our focus is
single-image reconstruction of compositional scenes, where object
geometry and relative placement must jointly explain the observation.

blocks.en: 3  Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: 3.1  Overview
blocks.zh: 3.1 概览

blocks.en:
Bri3D transfers the strong geometry and appearance priors of a
pre-trained single-object generator to compositional scene generation
through a unified, instance-aware scene scaffold. Rather than generating
objects independently and relying primarily on inter-instance
interactions, Bri3D first establishes their coarse geometry and spatial
arrangements within a shared scene representation. It contains two
trainable modules: a Scene Scaffold Generator 𝒢 S \mathcal{G}_{S} , which predicts a color-coded voxel scaffold for all
foreground objects, and an Anchored Voxel Refiner ℛ A \mathcal{R}_{A} , which converts each scaffold-derived object cluster
into a high-resolution voxel support compatible with the pre-trained
object generator.
The key to our design is to use voxel structure as the interface
between scene-level spatial organization and object-level detail
synthesis. The scene scaffold establishes coarse object geometry
and spatial relationships in a shared coordinate system, providing
structural anchors for subsequent refinement. Guided by these anchors
and object-specific image evidence, the Anchored Voxel
Refiner recovers finer object geometry within the spatial reference
established by the scaffold. The refined voxel supports
then condition a frozen detail-synthesis module from a pre-trained
object generator [ 39 ] to produce detailed
geometry and appearance. Finally, the generated objects are mapped
back into the shared scene using their scaffold-derived spatial
transformations. This design allows Bri3D to learn scene organization
and anchored geometry refinement while reusing pre-trained
object-level priors for detail synthesis.

blocks.en: 4.1  Experimental Setup

blocks.en:
Implementation details. Bri3D trains a Scene Scaffold Generator and an Anchored Voxel Refiner using Objaverse-XL [ 9 ] and 3D-FRONT [ 12 ] . Each 3D-FRONT instance is assigned a unique color, while Objaverse-XL objects are partitioned into 1–6 K-means clusters with distinct colors to construct structure-color supervision. An SC-VAE encodes and reconstructs these color-coded voxel structures with rasterization-based rendering losses, providing latents for both scaffold generation and object refinement. The generator predicts a 128 3 128^{3} instance-aware scaffold, and the refiner converts each object cluster into a prior-compatible 64 3 64^{3} voxel structure. Random occluders improve robustness to partial observations. Bri3D reconstructs foreground objects and their layouts, excluding floors, walls, and ceilings. Scene-level training follows MIDI’s 3D-FRONT split [ 18 ] ,
drawn from its cleaned corpus of approximately 15,000 scenes.
Separately, the object-level data construction uses 500,000 single-object
instances to provide coarse conditions and GT targets for refinement.
Both the Scene Scaffold Generator and Anchored Voxel Refiner are trained
for 10 epochs on 16 NVIDIA H20 GPUs, using AdamW with a learning rate
of 1 × 10 − 4 1\times 10^{-4} and a per-GPU batch size of 4.

Evaluation metrics. We evaluate geometry, layout, and visual quality following existing 3D scene generation methods [ 18 , 28 ] . Geometric fidelity is measured using Chamfer Distance (CD) and F-Score, computed at both the scene and object levels. We use CD-S/CD-O and F-S/F-O for scene/object metrics throughout; all reported CD values are scaled by 100 100 , and F-S/F-O are percentages. Spatial layout accuracy is assessed using the Intersection over Union
(BBox IoU) between corresponding axis-aligned bounding boxes in the
generated and ground-truth scenes. For Bri3D, BBox IoU evaluates the
scaffold-derived anchor boxes, which are retained through refinement
and detail synthesis. Collision rate is the percentage of object pairs
whose voxelized occupancies overlap in shared scene coordinates. For
Bri3D, scaffold instances are extracted and voxelized separately before
refinement; collisions are measured between these instance volumes. For visual quality, we compare rendered views of the generated scenes with corresponding ground-truth images to evaluate texture realism and perceptual fidelity.
Multiple perceptual metrics are reported, including PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS [ 45 ] , FID [ 15 ] , CLIP similarity [ 33 ] , and DINOv2 similarity [ 31 ] .

Baselines. We compare Bri3D against representative 3D scene generation methods: PartCrafter [ 24 ] , DepR [ 47 ] , Gen3DSR [ 1 ] , MIDI [ 18 ] , SceneGen [ 28 ] , and SAM3D [ 3 ] .
Since PartCrafter and DepR do not support texture rendering, we exclude them from visual-quality evaluation.
In-domain quantitative evaluation uses MIDI’s released 3D-FRONT [ 12 , 18 ] test split of 1,000 images, with the corresponding 3D scenes and instance masks. Consistent with the evaluation protocol of MIDI [ 18 ] , we use the instance segmentation masks provided by the dataset, rather than masks predicted by an off-the-shelf segmentor, as the segmentation input for standard quantitative comparisons. The robustness of Bri3D to erroneous segmentation maps is further analyzed in our ablation study (Fig. 8 ). For cross-dataset evaluation, we manually select 300 scenes: 150 from
HSSD [ 20 ] and 150 independently collected from
the BlendSwap platform [ 2 ] . We render multiple input views
per scene ourselves, pairing each view with its GT 3D scene; each
reconstruction uses one input image, so 300 denotes the number of scenes,
not the number of input views. ScanNet [ 7 ] , which lacks
complete ground truth, is used for qualitative evaluation.

Table 2 further demonstrate strong

similarity, while SAM3D obtains the second-best results. These results
indicate that the scene-anchor representation effectively transfers
object-level generative priors beyond the training distribution. As shown in Fig. 4 , Bri3D also generalizes to diverse room
layouts with heavy occlusions and incomplete observations, producing
high-fidelity reconstructions under challenging viewing conditions.

functions and furniture configurations.

blocks.en: 4.3  Scene Scaffold Generation

blocks.en:
A well-structured spatial layout is crucial for complete and realistic 3D scene generation. Our method supports independent layout prediction.
To evaluate the effectiveness of our Scene Scaffold Generator 𝒢 S \mathcal{G}_{S} , we report both quantitative and qualitative results in Table 3 and Fig. 5 (a), respectively. As shown in Table 3 , our G S G_{S} achieves a BBox IoU of 0.6732 in the 11–20 object range, significantly outperforming SAM3D [ 3 ] and MIDI [ 18 ] .
In terms of efficiency, Bri3D produces a scene layout directly
through scene scaffold prediction, taking only 5.1 s on a
NVIDIA A800 GPU for scenes with 1–10 objects. The scaffold already
provides the coarse geometry, instance organization, and spatial
reference needed for object refinement. Subsequent object refinement and detail
synthesis require an additional 37.5 s on average, bringing
the total reconstruction time to 42.6 s per scene.
For full scene reconstruction, Bri3D is approximately 3.2 × 3.2\times faster than SceneGen (135.0 s) and 1.5 × 1.5\times faster than SAM3D (64.1 s). For scenes with 11–20 objects,
scaffold prediction takes 5.2 s and full generation takes 78.4 s,
compared with 230.2 s for SceneGen and 179.6 s for SAM3D.
As shown in Fig. 5 (b), Bri3D exhibits two
failure modes: (1) under extreme clutter or ambiguous layouts,
it may incorrectly merge distinct objects; and (2) in highly
dense scenes with more than 30 objects, it may omit some
instances.

blocks.en: 5  Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented Bri3D, a scene-anchored compositional 3D generation framework that achieves coherent spatial layouts and fine-grained object geometry. Bri3D connects scene-level structural reasoning with object-level generative priors through a unified scene scaffold and anchored object refinement. By separating global scene organization from object-scale synthesis, scene-level training focuses on spatial organization and anchor refinement while reusing pretrained priors for detailed geometry and appearance. Through the proposed scene anchors and anchored voxel refinement, Bri3D produces more coordinated and unified scene reconstructions. Experiments demonstrate improvements in scene structure, object geometry, and visual quality. Scene scaffold prediction provides layouts in about five seconds; full scene generation is faster than SceneGen and SAM3D.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了Bri3D,一个场景所选择的构成的3D生成框架,实现了连贯的空间布局和精细的物体几何. Bri3D通过统一的场景脚手脚和锚定的物体精细化,将场景级结构推理与对象级基因前缀相接. 通过将全球场景组织与对象尺度合成区分开来,场景级培训侧重于空间组织和锚地精炼,同时重新使用预先被训练的前科进行详细的几何和外观. Bri3D通过拟议的场景锚地和锚地活塞精细化,产生更加协调和统一的场景重建. 实验展示了场景结构,物体几何,和视觉质量的改善. 场景脚手架预测在大约5秒内提供布局;完整的场景生成速度快于场景Gen和SAM3D.

blocks.en: B.1  Data Construction
blocks.zh: B.1 数据建设

blocks.en: We utilize the Objaverse-XL [ 9 ] and 3D-FRONT [ 12 ] datasets to construct our training corpus. Ground truth representations are prepared as color-coded voxel grids to supervise the SC-VAE. Training combines image conditioning with voxel and rendering supervision: 1. View-Consistent Supervision: We render ground-truth 3D scenes from the input camera pose to produce the RGB view and its color-coded instance label map. Both images condition the Scene Scaffold Generator ; only the color-coded instance label map supervises the rendering consistency loss ( ℒ render \mathcal{L}_{\text{render}} ). 2. Latent Space Supervision: The 4-channel color-coded voxel grids serve as the direct reconstruction target for the SC-VAE, providing dense supervision for learning the structured latent prior.
blocks.zh: 我们利用Objaverse-XL[9]和3D-FRONT[12]数据集来构建我们的训练大纲. 地面真实表示作为色码的活塞格来准备,以监督SC-VAE. 培训将图像调节与活塞和渲染监督结合起来: 1. 保持视图一致性 监督: 我们从输入相机的外观中制作出地面真实的3D场景,以生成RGB视图及其色码实例标签映射. 两个图像都对 Scene 脚手架生成器(Scene Scafold Generator)附加了条件;只有颜色编码的实例标签映射来监督渲染一致性损失(L compare\mathcal{L}_{\text{render}). 2. 后期空间监督: 由4个道组成的彩色编码Voxel网格作为SC-VAE的直接重建目标,为学习结构化后期潜入提供密集的监督.
